objective_for_doctor: A 58-year-old M patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: nausea.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I feel nauseous and like vomiting. I’m also having heavy, scary pain (intensity 7/10) in the lower chest and both sides of the chest/breasts that radiates up to my under the jaw and trachea, and to my shoulders (right and left).

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did the nausea and this 7/10 chest/breast pain start, and is the pain worse with exertion or breathing (and do you have sweating, shortness of breath, or faintness)?  
Doctor: Also, have you had vomiting, trouble swallowing, fever/cough, heartburn/acid taste, or any recent heavy meals/alcohol?

I don’t know.  

I can say the pain is heavy and scary, and it’s in my lower chest and both sides of the chest/breasts (right and left), radiating up to my under the jaw and trachea, and to both shoulders. I’m also feeling nauseous and like vomiting.

Doctor: Given the jaw/shoulder radiation with nausea, I’m worried about a heart problem—do you currently have shortness of breath, sweating, or dizziness, and are you able to reproduce the pain by pressing on your chest or moving your arms?  
Doctor: Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, high cholesterol, or prior heart disease?

I don’t know.

I have high blood pressure, diabetes, I smoke cigarettes, and I have high cholesterol (or I take medications to treat high cholesterol). I’ve had a heart attack or angina (chest pain). I’m also significantly overweight compared to people of the same height as I. I have close family members who had a cardiovascular disease problem before the age of 50.

Doctor: With your risk factors (HTN, diabetes, smoking, high cholesterol, prior angina/MI, obesity, and strong family history) and jaw/shoulder radiation plus nausea, I’m treating this as possible **acute coronary syndrome/heart attack**—do you have any shortness of breath, cold sweat, or feeling faint right now, and has the pain been going on more than 20 minutes?  
Doctor: If you can, take a deep breath—does it worsen sharply with breathing—and do you have any leg swelling or recent long travel/immobility?

Doctor: I’m concerned enough about a heart attack that we can’t wait—can you tell me if the chest/jaw/shoulder pain is constant or comes and goes, and what your current vital signs are if you can check (heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation)?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: 12-lead_ECG (STAT)  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: High_Sensitivity_Troponin (STAT)

Doctor: I need to decide this quickly—right now, please answer: is the chest/jaw/shoulder pain **constant** or **comes and goes**, and can you rate whether it’s **still severe (≥7/10)** after resting?  
Doctor: Also, I’m going to check vitals immediately—can you tell me your **blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation** (if available) while I arrange emergency care?
